query: How does resolution duration vary across incident category and priority?

per_column.name: resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: This is simply the focus variable itself expressed in hours. It is not an external associational variable; it restates resolution_duration and cannot be compared against the focus.

per_column.name: duration_band
per_column.rationale: Short/medium/long bands are a discretization of the focus variable, not an external segmenting variable. Interpretable categories, but grouping the focus by itself yields no informative relationship.

per_column.name: duration_vs_category_median
per_column.rationale: A deviation of the focus from its own category median. This is a transform of the focus, not an independent variable to segment on. Values are fine-grained near-continuous residuals with no interpretable categories.

per_column.name: duration_vs_priority_median
per_column.rationale: Same issue: a residual of the focus against its priority-group median. It is a re-expression of the focus, and its continuous values do not form well-separated, comparable categories.

per_column.name: duration_z_score
per_column.rationale: A standardized version of the focus variable itself. Opaque continuous score that restates the focus rather than opening a relationship with an external dimension.

judge.rationale: Every added column is a transformation, rescaling, binning, or residual of resolution_duration itself. None introduces an external, associational variable that a human could segment on and compare against the focus (the actual segmenting dimensions category and priority already exist in the original table). Several columns are fine-grained continuous residuals/z-scores that offer no interpretable, well-separated categories. As a set they fail the exploratory-analysis claim: they restate the focus rather than exposing informative relationships around it.
